title: Three methods: calendar, band, calendar + band
objectives: Compare the three methods on rule, strength and weakness.
Say which is the suggested default and when to check early.
body_md:
Three methods.

| Method | Rule | Strength | Weakness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Calendar | Check and rebalance on a fixed date, e.g. once a year | Simple; easy to explain and remember | May act on tiny drifts, or miss a big mid-year move |
| Band (threshold) | Act only when an asset drifts beyond a limit, e.g. ±5 points | Acts only when it matters | Needs regular monitoring |
| Calendar + band | Check yearly; act only if drift is beyond the band | Combines both; our suggested default | Slightly more to explain |

After a sharp market move (a fall of 15–20% or more), check the bands early rather than waiting for the calendar date.
example: Calendar: simple, but may act on tiny drifts or miss a big mid-year move. Band: acts only when it matters, but needs monitoring. Calendar + band: check yearly, act only beyond the band — the suggested default.
say: Calendar + band is the suggested default.
After a sharp fall of 15–20% or more, check bands early.
never: Calendar alone is the suggested default.

check.q: Which is our suggested default method?
check.why: Calendar + band. Check yearly; act only beyond the band.

check.q: With a ±5-point band, a 60% target at 64.6% means:
check.why: With a ±5-point band, a 60% target at 64.6% means within band: no action needed. Optional nudge with new money.

check.q: After a sharp market move, you should:
o: Check the bands early rather than waiting for the calendar date
check.why: After a sharp market move (a fall of 15–20% or more), check the bands early rather than waiting for the calendar date.
